official_measurement_examples.name: Two certificate types
official_measurement_examples.fact: Sections 191 and 192 distinguish certificates for existing matters from certificates for proposed use or operations.

official_measurement_examples.name: Existing certificate date
official_measurement_examples.fact: An existing-use certificate states lawfulness by reference to the state of affairs at the application date; it is not a fresh planning permission.

official_measurement_examples.name: Proposed certificate change risk
official_measurement_examples.fact: A proposed certificate can cease to protect a proposal if a material change in law or relevant circumstances occurs before development begins.

official_measurement_examples.name: Certificate precision
official_measurement_examples.fact: The certificate must define the lawful use, operation or matter precisely; a broad label must not be expanded beyond its terms.

official_measurement_examples.name: Conditions remain relevant
official_measurement_examples.fact: An LDC based on an extant permission does not erase conditions or limitations except to the extent specifically established by the certificate.

official_measurement_examples.name: Prior approval separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Prior approval and a lawful development certificate answer different legal questions and must not be treated as interchangeable.

official_measurement_examples.name: Planning permission separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: An LDC confirms lawfulness for planning control; it is not equivalent to granting a new planning permission.

official_measurement_examples.name: Parcel limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: An LDC does not establish ownership, access rights, building-regulations compliance or final development yield.

core_rules: LDC existing and proposed routes remain distinct
LDC is not new planning permission
certificate scope must be read precisely
existing certificate date must be retained
proposed certificate can be affected by material change
conditions are not erased unless specifically covered
LDC does not establish building regulations compliance
LDC does not establish title or easements
use-class label alone is not full certificate scope
evidence burden depends on certificate type
appeal rights do not imply certificate grant
no parcel clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
